summary: The map can become a second, stale architecture that consumes attention without improving outcomes, especially where the repository is small or the information is already discoverable from build metadata.

points.text: Hand-maintained dependency, feature and ownership data duplicates authoritative build files and source history; silent divergence can make an agent more confidently wrong than ordinary search would.
A universal schema tends either to omit domain-specific relationships or to grow into a catalog platform whose maintenance cost exceeds its navigation benefit.
Ownership data may encode formal team boundaries but miss actual expertise, temporary rotations and shared responsibility; enforcing it mechanically can bottleneck reviews.
For a compact, conventionally structured repository, directory names, tests and build graph may already provide enough orientation, making another entry point redundant.
